title: Night Horse Raids Turn Pursuit into Highway War

blocks.text: Acting on that resolve, the Singhs infiltrated the Mughal camp at night and seized the horses from the Mughals’ camp before the enemy fully understood what was happening. Those who resisted were cut down, and each successful raid weakened and depleted the Mughal force.

When larger detachments pressed back, the Sikhs vanished into marsh, brush, and cane, learning to camouflage themselves among the thick reeds until pursuit lost coherence. They turned concealment into a weapon and reappeared only when striking conditions favoured them.

From there the campaign broadened beyond survival into disruption of imperial movement itself. The Singhs began harrying the main highways to Delhi, Lahore, and Peshawar, showing that even when hounded from fixed ground they could still make the roads of empire unsafe.
